llm.label: ML & NLP papers
llm.note: 36 arXiv papers. Calibrated: at 0.0 the gate wrongly refuses 1 of 66 answerable questions (1.5%) and catches 9 of 18 adversarial. Lowering costs more catching than it recovers here, which is why this corpus kept the value the whole project was built on.

birds.label: Ornithology
birds.note: 45 Wikipedia documents, mixed .docx/.pptx/.xlsx/.pdf. Recalibrated 2026-08-26 and the reason it moved is worth more than the value: -3.0 was derived from confidences measured at rerank blend 0.00, and this corpus ships 0.20, so the gate had been calibrated against a pipeline the server does not run. Re-measured on the served pipeline, -3.0 is dominated. Every threshold in (-6.48, -4.55] catches the same five of six adversarial cases and wrongly refuses three of twenty-six rather than four, recovering bird-incubation for nothing. -5.5 is the middle of that interval: 0.95 of margin before it refuses an answerable question, 0.98 before it stops catching an adversarial one. An edge of the interval fits the threshold to one case. For scale, the ML papers' 0.0 wrongly refuses ten of the twenty-six here. What this does NOT fix: bird-dawn-chorus at -10.68 and bird-imprinting at -8.28 are questions whose answer the pipeline retrieved into the top five and whose passage the cross-encoder then scored below three of the six adversarial cases. No threshold recovers those without losing catches -- that is the reranker's calibration, not the gate's. Reranking keeps 20% of the first stage's ordering here (rerank_blend), which the other two corpora measured worse with: any-hit 0.808 -> 0.846 and MRR 0.570 -> 0.613, against -1.5 and -2.9 any-hit on the ML and quant sets at the same weight. On 26 cases the any-hit gain is one question, so MRR is the more trustworthy half of that.

quant.label: Quantitative finance
quant.note: 35 arXiv q-fin papers. Recalibrated 2026-08-26 after the golden set was rewritten: -6, -5 and -4 all catch every one of the six adversarial cases and wrongly refuse the same three of thirty-five, so the shipped -4 stands. At 0.0 it would refuse eleven. The earlier note claimed 0.0 refused nineteen of thirty-five; that was measured against a golden set asking textbook definitional questions this corpus never answers, and those questions scored low because they were unanswerable, not because the threshold was wrong. Answerable questions now score a median of +2.34, against -0.38 before.
